records.question: When should I apply for it?
history: What is the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
**You can file up to 90 days before your Post-Completion OPT end date.** USCIS must receive your application before your current OPT EAD card expires, or you won't be eligible for the extension.

**Key timing points:**
- **Send your documents to ISSS no later than 30 days before your OPT EAD end date**, to allow time for processing and mailing.
- **USCIS must receive your application within 60 days of the date ISSS prints your STEM OPT Request I-20.** If it arrives later, you'll need to redo the application.
- If you apply on time and your OPT EAD expires while the application is pending, you may keep working for up to 180 days past the expiration date, with your valid I-797 receipt notice.

In practice, that means starting roughly 90 to 30 days before your OPT end date. Check your own end date on your EAD card to work out your window.

If USCIS sends a Request for Evidence or returns your I-765, contact ISSS immediately, since response time is limited. For advice on your specific dates, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

Sources:
- [STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension)
- [Optional Practical Training (OPT)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)

records.question: Can I travel abroad while it's pending?
history: How long does it take USCIS to approve it?
records.search_query: Can I travel abroad while OPT is pending?
records.answer:
It depends on which type of OPT you've applied for. ISSS says:

**Pre-Completion OPT:** You may travel and re-enter under the general F-1 travel requirements.

**Post-Completion OPT, before you complete your degree** (and you're returning to resume studies): the general F-1 travel requirements apply.

**Post-Completion OPT, after degree completion (during the 60-day grace period):** Traveling before your OPT is approved "may be slightly risky." The F-1 regulations don't directly address this, but most students have re-entered successfully with a copy of the USCIS OPT Receipt Notice.

If you travel, carry:
- Valid passport
- Valid F-1 visa sticker (Canadian and Bermudian citizens are exempt)
- I-20 with OPT recommendation and a travel signature on page 2 that is no more than 6 months old
- OPT Receipt Notice (mailed 2-3 weeks after USCIS receives your application)

**STEM OPT pending:** You should be able to re-enter if your current OPT hasn't expired. If it has expired, travel may be risky. ISSS can't guarantee entry, since the Customs and Border Protection officer decides. You'd also need the items above (with the STEM OPT I-20 recommendation), plus your expired OPT EAD and a letter from your STEM employer.

**Note:** A January 2026 ISSS announcement says USCIS placed a hold on pending applications for people from certain travel ban countries, including OPT and STEM OPT. If this may apply to you, contact ISSS.

Because travel decisions affect your status, please talk with an ISSS advisor before you go.

Sources: [OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt), [STEM OPT Extension page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension), [USCIS hold announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/January/USCIS-issues-a-policy-memorandum-that-places-a-hold-on-all-pending-applications-for-individuals-from)
